title: Assistant action reveal state is not reset when the message changes
reasoning: AssistantMessageActions intentionally delays showing controls for a visible message, and the effect reruns when messageId changes. However, it only resets isRevealed when visible is false. If the same component instance receives a different messageId after the controls have already been revealed, isRevealed stays true until the new timer fires, so the new message bypasses the 2 second reveal delay. This can happen when a renderer reuses the component instance across message data changes, such as virtualization, replacement, or non-keyed list updates.
reproduction: Render AssistantMessageActions with visible=true, wait past ACTION_REVEAL_DELAY_MS so actions are shown, then rerender the same instance with a different messageId and visible=true. The action buttons remain visible immediately instead of returning to the placeholder state for the new message.
recommendation: Reset isRevealed to false whenever a new visible messageId starts a reveal cycle, before scheduling the timer. Keep the existing visible=false reset and cleanup behavior.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for this component, and the current excerpts do not show a rerender test that changes messageId on an already revealed action group.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a React Testing Library test that renders AssistantMessageActions, advances timers to reveal actions, rerenders with a new messageId while visible remains true, and asserts that the placeholder is restored until the delay elapses again.
